summary: The CLI count controls the host's repeated kernel launches over a grid sized to cover all rows. Each row's CSR interval feeds a retained multiply-add traversal and writes its row output. The compiled host loop retains its iteration backedge and synchronizes before stopping the timer; final SASS retains both the within-row loop and row bound/store.

source_evidence.claim: Thread/block mapping covers rows below dim; each active row traverses rowDelimiters[i]..rowDelimiters[i+1] accumulating val[j]*vec[cols[j]] then stores out[i]. CLI parses iterations and initializes nItems, CSR and operands; timed loop launches for each iteration, synchronizes and copies the final vector.
Build selects the CUDA implementation with optimization enabled.

compiled_evidence.claim: The timed section begins at clock call line 1293; the loop count is tested at 1300, launch occurs at 1370, counter comparison/backedge at 1372-1376 returns to b353, then device synchronization at 1378 precedes stop-clock call 1385.

compiled_evidence.claim: Row index is compared to dim at 0x0040 and out-of-range threads exit at 0x0050. The 0x0100 branch tests an empty CSR interval, not a row bound. DFMA at 0x0270 and nonzero backedges 0x0280->0x01d0 and 0x0db0->0x0590 retain the CSR work; STG at 0x14a0 writes output. This entire SASS dump is byte-identical to the independently inspected Beam hybrid r1 dump.

primary_quality_check.method: Independent full Fable r3 source, timed host flow and complete SASS; Haiku r1 full source, timed host flow and each architecture's cited arithmetic/backedge/store/guard checks. Separately inspected all four Beam timed host loops. Exact-byte comparisons show Beam r2-r5 SASS identical to independently inspected hybrid r1, and Fable r1/r2/r4/r5 SASS identical to r3. Other cases retain the independent Luna source review.
